headlines.title: How Investors May Respond To Netflix (NFLX) Big Investors Split
headlines.summary: Netflix faces renewed scrutiny as high-profile investors Bill Ackman and Michael Burry take opposing valuation stances while the business manages slowing revenue growth, softer advertising expectations and potential live sports content costs. The real story for Netflix now is less about subscriber scale and more about how effectively management converts pricing, ads and buybacks into durable free cash flow despite rising competition.

headlines.title: Bill Ackman Likes Netflix Under $60. Michael Burry Is Waiting for the High $30s. Who’s Right?
headlines.summary: Key TakeawaysNetflix is down 45% this year. Bill Ackman likes it below $60, while Michael Burry is waiting for the high $30s.

headlines.title: Netflix Needs 'Buzzy' Franchises
headlines.summary: Despite being impacted by weakening viewer engagement, Netflix has the financial wherewithal to up its game with major brand franchises and prized intellectual property.

description: Netflix, Inc. provides entertainment services worldwide. The company offers television (TV) series, documentaries, feature films, games, and live programming across various genres and languages. It also provides members the ability to receive streaming content through a host of internet-connected devices, including TVs, digital video players, TV set-top boxes, and mobile devices. Netflix, Inc. was incorporated in 1997 and is headquartered in Los Gatos, California.
